newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudis edge close to 700,000 T barley purchase.
newsitem.headline: Saudis edge close to 700,000 T barley purchase.

text.p: Saudi Arabia, in negotiations to purchase barley, is moving towards buying 700,000 tonnes of the grain for July delivery but traders said the deals had not yet been finally worked out.
Traders said there were signs the barley would be bought at around $164 to $171 per tonne including freight, following a tender on Monday, but the prices had not been confirmed.
"Nobody has had a confirmation out of Saudi Arabia but it looks likely to happen around these numbers," one trader said.
Saudi Arabia tendered on Monday for 450,000 tonnes of optional-origin feed barley to be delivered to Jeddah and 250,000 tonnes to Dammam, both by July 15.
Traders disagreed about the likely origin of the grain, with several putting Canada out in front to supply the barley but others counting on up to 300,000 tonnes from the European Union.

The EU granted export subsidies for 89,200 tonnes of barley to cover existing business at its last weekly export tender and some officials have suggested the season is just about over after a sharp jump in exports from the previous campaign.
On a separate front, Iran is expected to start reviewing offers to supply 100,000 tonnes of feed barley with August shipment during the next few hours, traders said.
